history_of_present_illness.text: Patient presents with fever, cough, body pain, and fatigue for 3 days. Fever was initially mild, then spiked to 101 °F yesterday evening. Took Paracetamol 650 mg twice yesterday, which temporarily reduced fever. Cough is mostly dry, occasionally with a little mucus. Patient reports slight breathlessness on climbing stairs. Denies chest pain, wheezing, severe shortness of breath, loss of smell or taste, vomiting, diarrhea, abdominal pain, or burning during urination. Patient had contact with an office colleague who had a viral fever last week.
items: Took Paracetamol 650 mg twice yesterday with temporary relief

family_history.text: Father has diabetes. Mother has hypertension.

drug_allergy.text: Allergic to Penicillin, develops a skin rash after taking it.

clinical_examination.text: Current vitals: Temperature 100.8 °F, BP 132/84 mmHg, Pulse 92/min, SpO2 98%, Weight 74 kg. Patient appears conscious, oriented, mildly febrile, and not in respiratory distress. No swelling or rashes noted. Respiratory system appears mildly affected with an upper respiratory tract infection. No concerning cardiac, abdominal, or neurological symptoms are present from history.
